output_list.criticism: The 'reward' function has an integer overflow vulnerability. When 'locked' is true, it performs a 'require(totalLockedRewardsOf[_to] + _value > totalLockedRewardsOf[_to])'' check. However, if 'totalLockedRewardsOf[_to]' is at its maximum value, adding _value can cause an overflow and become 'false'. This can be exploited to locked additional unauthorized rewards for any target user via the 'reward' function call.

The 'transferReward' function has an integer overflow where it performs a 'require(totalLockedRewardsOf[addr] > _value)'' check. If 'totalLockedRewardsOf[addr]' is at its minimum value and '_value' is non-zero, a overflow in 'totalLockedRewardsOf[addr] -= _value' can occur, making the check always 'false'. This vulnerability can be exploited to locked additional unauthorized rewards for any target user via the 'transferReward' function call.

The 'unlockReward' function has an integer overflow where it performs a 'require(totalLockedRewardsOf[addr] > _value)'' check. If 'totalLockedRewardsOf[addr]' is at its minimum value and '_value' is non-zero, a overflow in 'totalLockedRewardsOf[addr] -= _value' can occur, making the check always 'false'. This vulnerability can be exploited to unlock additional unauthorized rewards for any target user via the 'unlockReward' function call.

The 'setAdmin' function has a access control vulnerability. It uses 'admin[addr]=enabled' to assign admin rights, allowing anyone to call this function and gain admin privileges, potentially causing unexpected financial losses for asset owners.

The 'setUsersCanTrade' function has a access control vulnerability. It allows anyone to call this function and modify the trade state, potentially leading to unexpected financial losses for asset owners.
